title: Configuration for CLI Tools
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of configuration for cli tools in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply configuration for cli tools in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to avoiding hard-coded secrets and paths and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Configuration for CLI Tools through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding configuration for cli tools helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Configuration for CLI Tools helps you reason about environment variables. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Environment variables. Then connect it to Configuration files. The remaining syllabus points—Command-line overrides, Avoiding hard-coded secrets and paths—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports configuration for cli tools. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for configuration for cli tools using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Avoiding hard-coded secrets and paths), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` or `ruby lesson.rb data.csv`. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain configuration for cli tools, identify its place in command-line applications and automation, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
